name: Colossus
reason: gate passed; run with --promote to apply
evidence_url: The xAI Colossus supercomputer is located at 3231 Paul R. Lowry Road in South Memphis, Tennessee, in a 785,000 square foot former Electrolux manufacturing facility situated on over 217 acres. An affiliate of Phoenix Investors acquired the building in December 2023. By March 2024 the property was leased to xAI. They took over the factory with the goal of building the world's largest supercomputer, named Colossus, to fuel artificial intelligence, with more than a dozen generators steadily burning methane gas visible at the site as early as September 2024. In November 2024, TVA approved xAI's request for over 100 MW of grid power supplied through MLGW, upgrading from an initial grid connection of only 8 MW (local news asserts Musk has said the site needs 150 MW). xAI submitted a contract to purchase 13 acres of City of Memphis-owned land at 2685 Plant Road, located on the south side of the T.E. Maxson Wastewater Treatment Facility, through its affiliate CTC Property LLC, for $820,000. The proposed Colossus Water Recycling Plant will process municipal wastewater from the T.E. Maxson Wastewater Treatment Plant with a planned capacity of 10.4 million gallons per day. TVA and Nucor Steel have signed Letters of Intent to purchase water from the facility alongside xAI, with peak demand by all three facilities estimated at 12.5 million gallons per day.

name: Colossus 2
reason: gate passed; run with --promote to apply
evidence_url: This project shares its history with Colossus, and is an expansion of the initial site, located at 5420 Tulane Road. The facility, previously a 1,000,000 square foot warehouse owned by Coliers and built in late 2023. MZX TECH LLC, an affiliate of xAI, purchased the site in February 2025 for about $80 million. Based on satellite imagery and analysis of the cooling equipment, SemiAnalysis estimated Colossus 2 is progressing toward 400 MW of critical IT capacity, with a hybrid cooling system of approximately 130 dry coolers and 135 adiabatic cooling units, producing an estimated annual water footprint of approximately 346 million gallons per year (roughly 0.9 million gallons per day). By April 2025, aerial imagery showed 35 gas turbines operating at a combined 422 MW without permits, which the Southern Environmental Law Center stated makes the facility likely the largest industrial emitter of NOx in Memphis, setting a good estimate for its capacity.

The first 100 MW building reached full operational status in late 2025 across two phases. The campus is designed for a projected PUE of approximately 1.18 and near-zero water usage effectiveness.

name: Atlas Power Williston

The facility currently draws ~200–240 MW and employs more than 30 permanent workers. The project has faced noise complaints from neighboring properties, and Atlas Power has invested approximately $5 million in acoustic mitigation measures.
